existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: 'Commercial purpose' means the sale/resale of a record or use of its information to advance the requester's strategic business interests for profit, excluding news, citizen oversight, and academic/scientific/journalistic/public research.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: RAO must classify a request to set fee basis or evaluate a fee-waiver/excess-fee petition.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: as used in this section ''commercial purpose'' shall mean the sale or resale of any portion of the public record or the use of information from the public record to advance the requester's strategic business interests in a manner that the requester can reasonably expect to make a profit, and shall not include gathering or reporting news or gathering information to promote citizen oversight or further the understanding of the operation or activities of government or for academic, scientific, journalistic or public research or education
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Definition the software branches on: drives fee basis and eligibility for excess-fee/waiver treatment.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Reasonable fee not to exceed actual cost
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: A records access officer may assess a reasonable fee for production (except freely-inspectable records), and the fee shall not exceed the actual cost of reproducing the record.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: RAO produces records that are not freely available for inspection.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: A records access officer may assess a reasonable fee for the production of a public record except those records that are freely available for public inspection. The reasonable fee shall not exceed the actual cost of reproducing the record.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Overall ceiling under which the itemized fee components sit.

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: The fee for standard black-and-white paper copies or printouts shall not exceed 5 cents per page, for both single- and double-sided copies.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: the fee assessed for standard black and white paper copies or printouts of records shall not exceed 5 cents per page, for both single and double-sided black and white copies or printouts
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Ceiling $0.05/page. City may charge at or below.

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: The actual cost of any storage device or material provided in response to a request may be included as part of the fee.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: RAO provides records on a storage device/material.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: the actual cost of any storage device or material provided to a person in response to a request for public records under subsection (a) may be included as part of the fee

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: For a municipality, the hourly labor rate must equal or be less than the lowest-paid capable employee's rate and shall not exceed $25 per hour, unless a higher rate is approved by the Supervisor.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Municipality devotes more than 2 hours of employee time to a request.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: if a municipality is required to devote more than 2 hours of employee time to search for, compile, segregate, redact or reproduce a record requested, the records access officer may include as part of the fee an hourly rate equal to or less than the hourly rate attributed to the lowest paid employee who has the necessary skill required to search for, compile, segregate, redact or reproduce the record requested but the fee (A) shall not be more than $25 per hour unless such rate is approved by the supervisor of records under clause (iv)
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Municipal ceiling $25/hr; may be exceeded only with Supervisor approval (MA-0037).

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: For a (state) agency, the hourly labor rate must equal or be less than the lowest-paid capable employee's rate and shall not be more than $25 per hour.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Agency devotes more than 4 hours of employee time to a request.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: if an agency is required to devote more than 4 hours of employee time ... the records access officer may also include as part of the fee an hourly rate equal to or less than the hourly rate attributed to the lowest paid employee who has the necessary skill ... but the fee (A) shall not be more than $25 per hour
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Agency variant of the same ceiling concept (agency cannot exceed $25/hr even with approval).

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: For a municipality with a population over 20,000, no labor fee may be assessed for the first 2 hours of work performed.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: (B) shall not be assessed for the first 2 hours of work performed where the responding municipality has a population of over 20,000 people
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Free-hour threshold (2 hrs) applies only to municipalities over 20,000 population; municipalities of 20,000 or fewer are not entitled to charge labor at all under the structure and the 2-hour free tier is population-gated.

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: For a (state) agency, no labor fee may be assessed for the first 4 hours of work performed.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: (B) shall not be assessed for the first 4 hours of work performed
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Agency variant of the same free-hours concept (4 hrs).

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: A fee shall not be assessed for time spent segregating or redacting records unless such segregation/redaction is required by law or approved by the Supervisor.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Entity spends time segregating or redacting records.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: (C) shall not be assessed for time spent segregating or redacting records unless such segregation or redaction is required by law or approved by the supervisor of records under clause (iv)

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Supervisor approval for redaction charge / excess rate
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: The Supervisor may approve a petition to charge for segregation/redaction time, or a municipal petition to charge over $25/hour, if the request is for a commercial purpose or the fee is a necessary, reasonable good-faith cost not designed to deter access; the entity must furnish the petition to the requestor and the Supervisor decides within 5 business days.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Agency/municipality petitions the Supervisor to charge redaction time or exceed $25/hr.
existing_fee_payment_rules.clock_spec: Supervisor written determination within 5 business-days of receipt of the petition
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: the supervisor of records may approve a petition from an agency or municipality to charge for time spent segregating or redacting, or a petition from a municipality to charge in excess of $25 per hour, if the supervisor of records determines that (A) the request is for a commercial purpose; or (B) the fee represents an actual and good faith representation by the agency or municipality to comply with the request, the fee is necessary such that the request could not have been prudently completed without the redaction, segregation or fee in excess of $25 per hour and the amount of the fee is reasonable and the fee is not designed to limit, deter or prevent access
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Structural fee-petition path; the 5-business-day decision clock is stated in § 10(d)(iv)(3). Contains a multi-factor test kept intact per grain rule.

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: The RAO may waive or reduce a fee upon a showing that disclosure is in the public interest (likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of government and not primarily in the requestor's commercial interest), or that the requestor lacks the financial ability to pay the full reasonable fee.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Requestor shows public interest or inability to pay.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: the records access officer may waive or reduce the amount of any fee charged under this subsection upon a showing that disclosure of a requested record is in the public interest because it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of the operations or activities of the government and is not primarily in the commercial interest of the requestor, or upon a showing that the requestor lacks the financial ability to pay the full amount of the reasonable fee

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: If fees are to be assessed, the RAO must provide a written, itemized, good-faith estimate of fees before complying, within the 10-business-day response.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Fees will be charged for a request.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: if fees are being assessed, a records access officer shall provide a written, itemized, good faith estimate of any fees that may be charged to produce the records prior to complying with a public records request within ten business days.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: No fee unless timely written response
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: A records access officer shall not charge a fee for a public record unless the RAO responded to the requestor within 10 business days under subsection (b).
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: RAO failed to provide the § 10(b) response within 10 business days.
existing_fee_payment_rules.clock_spec: terminal: fee right is forfeited if no § 10(b) response within 10 business-days
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: A records access officer shall not charge a fee for a public record unless the records access officer responded to the requestor within 10 business days under subsection (b).
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Strong operational consequence tied to the response clock; regulatory parallel 950 CMR 32.06(2)(c). clock_effect terminal reflects the loss of the fee entitlement.

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: The RAO may deny public-records requests from a requester who has failed to compensate the entity for previously produced public records.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Requester has an unpaid balance for previously produced records.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: the records access officer may deny public records requests from a requester who has failed to compensate the agency or municipality for previously produced public records

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Payment of reasonable fee as precondition
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: The production duty is conditioned on the RAO receiving payment of a reasonable fee as set forth in subsection (d).
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: A fee is properly assessed for a request.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: (iii) the records access officer receives payment of a reasonable fee as set forth in subsection (d).

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: A records access officer may delay provision of records until all fees related to the request are paid in full by the person seeking access.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: a records access officer may delay provision of records until all fees related to such requests are paid in full by the person seeking access to the requested records in accordance with 950 CMR 32.07.
